Subject: Please reopen: PR #812 changed the default wavelength frame

I did read the changelog before posting. I have now traced the offset to PR #812, and the cause is a changed library default, not my wavelength calibration.

In 2.5.0, PR #812 changed the default in LineList.__init__ from wave_frame='air' to wave_frame='vacuum'. My optical spectra are calibrated in air, as I stated in the original post. Using vacuum rest wavelengths against those data explains both the direction and size of the shift: the vacuum/air wavelength ratio near H-alpha is approximately 1.00028, consistent with the redshift offset I reported, or about 83 km/s.

The workaround that fixes this for my data is to specify the frame explicitly:

LineList(..., wave_frame='air')

That setting is appropriate for air-calibrated spectra; it is not a blanket recommendation for every dataset.

I am frustrated that this was marked solved and attributed to my calibration without checking the frame handling. I spent two days investigating that suggestion, including re-reducing arc lamps for 40 spectra unnecessarily. Asking whether I had “actually read the changelog” was dismissive, particularly when the relevant entry only says “Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812).” That wording does not tell users that the default wavelength convention changed, and there was no deprecation warning.

“Works for me” does not rule out this regression. A meaningful comparison needs to establish the wavelength frame and configuration used. Data already in vacuum, or a radio workflow that does not exercise this optical air/vacuum mismatch, would not necessarily show my offset. I do not know which applies to your test. m_okonkwo also reported a possible offset here, which warrants follow-up rather than closure.

Please reopen this thread so maintainers can assess it. Please also add an explicit CHANGES.md entry describing the default change and migration workaround, or a warning when wave_frame is not set. Leaving the workaround here should help other users avoid the same unnecessary calibration checks.
